title: Adapt to new spec redesign and flow
description:
The specification for the app has changed and we are changing the complete way in which users interact. There's no need for backward compatibility as everything is started from scratch.

The new general flow follows the following:
1. authenticate - this is exactly the same as before
2. set user profile:
-  IF USER PROFILE IS MISSING ANY OF THE PIECES inside UserProfileModel (dob, gender, weight, height) then trigger `actionProfile`
- the whole process is described in `actionProfile.ts`
3. set user lifestyle
- IF USER PROFILE doesn't have 1 lifestyle in userProfile.lifestyles then trigger 'actionLifestyle'
- the whole process is described in `actionLifestyle.ts`
4. generate a macro goal:
- the whole process is described in `actionMacroGoal`
5. generate micro goals:
- the whole process is described in `actionMicroGoalsGenerate`
Overall flow is complete.
What's left is to update the `scheduler.ts` to send the two messages that `actionMacroGoal` generates for the checkins. The morning one triggers a new `actionMicroGoalsGenerate` and the evening one triggers a new `actionMicroGoalsCheck` .

features.title: Refactor `index.ts` to orchestrate the new user onboarding flow
features.description: Modify the main message handler in `index.ts`. Remove the command-based listeners for `/profile` and `/newgoal`. Implement a new, state-driven handler that, for every user message, checks the user's profile state and triggers the next required action in the onboarding sequence: `actionProfile`, `actionLifestyle`, `actionMacroGoal`, and `actionMicroGoalsGenerate`. The new flow should be the default behavior for any authenticated user who has not completed it.

features.title: Update scheduler to trigger morning micro-goal generation
features.description: Modify `src/lib/scheduler.ts`. The scheduler should identify the morning check-in created by `actionMacroGoal`. When this check-in is due for a user, instead of just sending a message, it must trigger the `actionMicroGoalsGenerate` flow for that user. This involves calling the appropriate function from `src/actions/actionMicroGoalsGenerate.ts`.

features.title: Update scheduler to trigger evening micro-goal check-in
features.description: Modify `src/lib/scheduler.ts`. The scheduler should identify the evening check-in created by `actionMacroGoal`. When this check-in is due for a user, it must trigger the `actionMicroGoalsCheck` flow. This involves calling the appropriate function from `src/actions/actionMicroGoalsCheck.ts`.

features.title: Action: Profile - interactive onboarding
features.description:
Implement the interactive profile setup flow in @src/actions/actionProfile.ts 

Scope:
- Detect missing fields: name, dob, gender, weight_raw or weight, height_raw or height via ProfilesService.profilesControllerMe().
- Step-by-step prompts with HTML formatting (parse_mode: 'HTML'):
  - Ask for name (free text). Validate non-empty; trim.
  - Ask for DOB (YYYY-MM-DD). Validate 4-2-2 pattern and reasonable date. Echo back parsed result on success.
  - Ask for gender with inline keyboard: 'Male', 'Female', 'Other'. Use callback_data starting with 'profile:gender:...'.
  - Ask for weight (accept free-form like '82 kg, 180 lb, 11st 4lb'). Store into weight_raw.
  - Ask for height (accept free-form like '175 cm, 1.75 m, 5\'11\''). Store into height_raw.
- Persist after each step with ProfilesService.profilesControllerUpdate().
- Maintain progress in session (lib/sessionStore) so the flow is resumable across messages.
- Clean up old inline keyboards after selection to reduce clutter (editMessageReplyMarkup to empty).
- On completion, send a short confirmation message and proceed to lifestyle flow by invoking actionLifestyle or by returning such that runOnboardingIfNeeded continues.
- Add callback_query handlers for 'profile:gender:*' in index.ts, consistent with the existing handler style.

Acceptance criteria:
- When profile is incomplete, the bot guides the user through all missing steps only, in order.
- Validations: name must be non-empty; DOB must match YYYY-MM-DD and be a valid date; gender must update via inline keyboard; weight/height captured as raw strings.
- Each successful step updates the backend; on error (e.g., invalid DOB), the bot re-prompts with guidance.
- Flow can resume if interrupted (progress stored in session).
- After completion, next step in the onboarding (lifestyle) is triggered or allowed to proceed per runOnboardingIfNeeded.

features.title: Action: Lifestyle - active and energy levels
features.description:
Implement the lifestyle capture flow in @src/actions/actionLifestyle.ts .

Scope:
- If userProfile.lifestyles is empty, prompt the user for two 1–5 scale inputs using inline keyboards with emoji labels:
  1) 'How active are you currently?' options: 1 '🛋️ Very low', 2 '🚶‍♂️ Light', 3 '🏃 Moderate', 4 '💪 High', 5 '🔥 Very high'
  2) 'How’s your energy and wellbeing today?' options: 1 '😴 Very low', 2 '😐 Low', 3 '🙂 Okay', 4 '😊 Good', 5 '🤩 Great'
- Use namespaced callback data like 'lifestyle:active:1..5' and 'lifestyle:energy:1..5'.
- Store both responses as a new lifestyle via ProfilesService.profilesControllerAddLifestyle({ activeLevel, energyLevel }).
- Prevent duplicate submissions; if the user already has at least one lifestyle, skip this flow.
- After saving, send a confirmation message and proceed to macro goal flow (invoke actionMacroGoal with firstGoal=true or allow runOnboardingIfNeeded to continue).
- Clean up the inline keyboards after selection (editMessageReplyMarkup to empty).
- Add callback_query handlers for 'lifestyle:*' in index.ts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Users see clearly labeled 1–5 options for each question via inline keyboards.
- Selecting both values results in a single ProfilesService.profilesControllerAddLifestyle call with correct integers (1–5).
- The flow does not re-ask if a lifestyle record already exists.
- After completion, the user is guided to the macro goal step.

features.title: Action: MacroGoal - suggestions, creation, and check-ins
features.description: Implement macro goal creation in @src/actions/actionMacroGoal.ts , including suggestions UI and check-in scheduling. Scope: - First-time entry (firstGoal=true): send a short intro like 'Got it — now let’s set your direction for the week.' - Prompt: ask the user to type a macro goal or send a voice message. Provide examples by fetching suggestions via GoalsService.goalsControllerGenerateMacroGoalSuggestions() and render them in a message with an inline keyboard to pick (callback namespace 'macro:suggest:'). - If the user sends audio/voice: download via downloadTelegramAudioFile and call GoalsService.goalsControllerCreateMacroGoalFromAudio. - If the user sends text or selects a suggestion: call GoalsService.goalsControllerCreateMacroGoalFromText. - While processing, send a 'Processing...' message to set expectations. - Clear old check-ins via CheckInsService.checkInsControllerClearCheckIns(). - Schedule two daily check-ins via CheckInsService.checkInsControllerAddCheckIn(): - Morning: next 09:00 local (tomorrow if past 09:00 today) with metadata.message like 'Morning Reminder!' and include metadata.chatId = chat.id. - Evening: next 19:00 local (tomorrow if past 19:00 today) with metadata.message like 'Evening Check in!' and include metadata.chatId = chat.id. - After scheduling, send a message explaining morning micro-goals and evening check-ins, then trigger actionMicroGoalsGenerate to produce the first set. - Ensure the undefined variable bug is fixed by using the actual chat.id for metadata.chatId. - Clean up any suggestion keyboards after selection. - Add callback_query handlers for 'macro:suggest:*' in index.ts. Acceptance criteria: - Users can pick a suggested macro goal, type their own, or send a voice note to create the macro goal; successful creation is acknowledged. - Existing check-ins are cleared and exactly two daily check-ins are created with the correct metadata (including chatId and messages containing 'Morning' or 'Evening'). - After creation, the user receives onboarding messaging and immediately gets their micro goals for the day via actionMicroGoalsGenerate. - No usage of undefined variables; chat.id is correctly persisted in check-in metadata.

features.title: Action: MicroGoalsGenerate - display today’s micro goals
features.description:
Implement micro goal generation messaging in @src/actions/actionMicroGoalsGenerate.ts .

Scope:
- Call GoalsService.goalsControllerGenerateMicroGoals() and capture the returned goals.
- Send a message: 'Here are your 3 micro goals for today.' and list each as a bullet with clear formatting (parse_mode 'HTML' optional).
- Follow up with: 'We will check in with you in the evening...' and mention '/journal' for optional journaling.
- Ensure the function returns true to indicate flow handled.

Acceptance criteria:
- After calling the action, the user sees exactly three micro goals listed in a readable format.
- The informational follow-up message about evening check-in and journaling is sent.
- The action is idempotent in the sense that running it twice immediately does not create duplicate UI keyboards or crash.

features.title: Action: MicroGoalsCheck - evening check-in UI
features.description:
Implement the evening micro-goals check-in flow in @src/actions/actionMicroGoalsCheck.ts .

Scope:
- Fetch current day ACTIVE micro goals (e.g., via GoalsService.goalsControllerListMicroGoalsByState or equivalent).
- Render a checklist-style message asking which were completed, with an inline keyboard row per goal showing toggle buttons (e.g., '✅ Done' / '❎ Not yet'), using callback data like 'microcheck:<goalId>:toggle'.
- Upon each toggle, update the micro goal state via the appropriate GoalsService endpoint (e.g., mark complete/incomplete) and re-render the keyboard to reflect the new state.
- When all three have been marked (or after the user indicates completion), send a message: 'Great! Thanks for these responses.' and optionally nudge journaling.
- Clean up the keyboard after completion to reduce clutter.
- Add callback_query handlers under 'microcheck:*' namespace in index.ts.

Acceptance criteria:
- The user receives an evening check-in prompt showing their three goals with per-goal toggle controls.
- Toggling a goal updates backend state and UI reflects the change without creating duplicate buttons.
- After all goals are addressed, the bot sends a closing message and removes the inline keyboard.

features.title: Scheduler: route macro goal check-ins to actions
features.description:
Finalize scheduler behavior in @src/lib/scheduler.ts  to act on check-ins created by actionMacroGoal.

Scope:
- Parse CheckInModel items hourly and extract message and chatId from metadata.
- If metadata.message contains 'Morning' (case-insensitive), trigger actionMicroGoalsGenerate for that user/chat instead of sending a plain text reminder.
- If metadata.message contains 'Evening' (case-insensitive), trigger actionMicroGoalsCheck for that user/chat.
- Use existing dedup mechanism to avoid multiple triggers within the same hour window.
- Ensure chatId resolution: prefer metadata.chatId numeric; otherwise support metadata.chat_id or metadata.telegram.chatId or metadata.telegram.chat.id. If missing, persist telegram metadata via update for future runs (best-effort).
- Maintain graceful error handling and continue processing other users.

Acceptance criteria:
- When actionMacroGoal schedules morning/evening check-ins, the scheduler recognizes them and invokes the correct actions at the scheduled hour.
- No duplicate triggers occur within a single hour run.
- If chatId is correctly stored by actionMacroGoal, the scheduler successfully routes without needing fallbacks.
- Logs indicate skipped items when chatId cannot be determined, without crashing the scheduler.

features.title: when doing actionLifestyle - show user choices
features.description:
as the user selects the options in @src/actions/actionLifestyle.ts after they've been selected - they disappear, so if the user looks back at the conversation they only see the bot messages.
We need to add the selection as a user message if possible, so they can see it clearly. If that's not possible - then the bot should send a message similar to how @src/actions/actionProfile.ts is done with Gender. (but if a message from the user can be sent - then we should do that instead for this case also. If the only way to do this is with the answers in the keyboard itself - let's do it).

after authenticating for the first time and starting the onboarding flow and triggering @src/actions/actionProfile.ts the user should see a message:
"Please tell us your name"

features.title: we need a test command to trigger an evening goal check
features.description: to be able to test the evening goal check, there should be a command like '/test-evening' that will trigger the same exact flow for the @src/lib/scheduler.ts as if the time has come for the evening check.

features.title: In the actionMicroGoalsCheck the UI needs updating
features.description:
First - always show all micro goals for the given macro goal - even if they've been marked as finished before.

Second - once the user marks all 3 goals, we should send this message:

“Would you like to leave a short voice note or type a few words about how the day felt?”

And now the user can reply with either text (behaving as if they triggered the /journal command) or a voice memo (behaving as if they triggered the /voice command).

features.title: There needs to be a new check in generated at the end of a week
features.description:
When generating a macro goal, apart from the morning and evening check-ins - there needs to be a checkin scheduled for a week ahead (so frequency weekly), an hour after the evening check in.

this should trigger a new flow that should be stored in its own file:
"actionWeeklyReset" .
The user should be shown this message:

    “This week you completed [X]% of your micro goals — great work 💪."

Where X will be the computed amount of all the micro goals for the given macro goal that is active.

Then a 2nd message right after it should fire saying:

"Would you like to set a new weekly goal or continue building on this one?”

    → Buttons: Continue | New Goal .
Continue will then essentially do nothing functionally other than send the message:
"Great! Keep up the good work!"

and selectiong "New Goal" will trigger a new @src/actions/actionMacroGoal.ts

features.title: when past the initial forced onboarding flow - any command cancels the previous
features.description: once the user has onboarded and got their first macro goal - i.e. is not forced to do anything, if they send a command like /start or /journal, then it should override the previous command. So if they send /journal and the app is waiting for them to submit text, but they type in /voice - then it should trigger the voice command.

features.title: Weight and Height needs to be captured in 1 message
features.description:
Currently in @src/index.ts we are capturing height and weight separately. This needs to be combined into 1 bot message and to be captured in 1 go from the user.
The message needs to say:
“Please tell me your weight and height (e.g., 77 kg, 178 cm).”
And when the user provides them (if there are no errors), we send back a confirmation:
"Got it — 77 kg / 178 cm."
And then move onto to the next flow.

features.title: Capture age instead of date of birth
features.description:
In @src/index.ts we capture the date of birth, but this is hard for a user to type. So asking for age is easier. The backend input expects a date, so we simply record today's date and subtract the age of the user as the input and pass it as the dob field (the saved string needs to be an ISO timestamp).
When the user submits, we confirm with (example for 46):

“Got it — 46. Thanks, that helps me understand your stage in life 💪.”

features.title: Journal entry saved user feedback
features.description:
After user posts a voice note:
- Transcribe and summarise the key points (1–2 sentences). Send back something like:
“You mentioned getting back into the gym and balancing that with time with your kids. Shall I record this, or do you want to re-record?”
So to get this done, the backend returns "response" that should be used as the first sentence and then we append the 2nd sentence.
- Add buttons: [✅ Submit]  [🔁 Re-record]. If re-record → clear previous entry and re-prompt. If submit → confirm:
“Journal entry saved ✅.”

features.title: Add sleep to sending messages
features.description: In multiple places there's a "TODO: add sleep of 2s" - this needs to be added in the same way in all those places. This is because there are multiple messages being sent there at once and it feels like a cascade when the user receives them so we need to pace them appropriately.

features.title: When showing macro goal suggestions, use the non-inline keyboard
features.description:
In @src/common/keyboards.ts we have keyboard uis made to accommodate user responses using them.
It uses this hidden character '‎' prepended to the front of the user presented input, and when the user selects it - we know how many of that character are present in the selection so we know how to proceed. If there's an easier way to do this in Telegram's methodology then we should do that, but if not, we should continue with this approach.
For this task @src/actions/actionMacroGoal.ts needs to change and show the 3 macro goal suggestions using this keyboard.

features.title: When doing the morning check in with the micro goals - first ask about the energy levels
features.description:
The same way as the user is asked about their energy levels and mood during onboarding, we need to ask the same before generating the new set of micro goals. This is so those micro goals can take into account the new energy levels.
Probably @src/lib/scheduler.ts and @src/actions/actionMicroGoalsGenerate.ts needs to change.
